creator: Claude
name: Crowbar
source_format: MagicaVoxel VOX v150 (SIZE, XYZI, RGBA), single model

derived.glb_note: Derived from the .vox by tools/claude/export_glb.py; do not edit by hand. Linear COLOR_0 vertex colours, one material.

resolution_rationale: 1.25 cm cells: a hand-sized pickup would be only 3-6 cells at 2.5 cm, losing the grip, cap or label that identifies it. A 2.5 cm hex bar is one cell at 2.5 cm, too thin to show the gooseneck's taper, the split claw or the flattened pry end; at 1.25 cm the bar is 2x2 cells and the hook is a smooth 8-cell curve. Matches the other small hand tools of the family.
godot_mapping: godot = ((vx - px) * s, (vz - pz) * s, -(vy - py) * s)
pivot_note: Bottom centre of the occupied footprint at ground level.
front_note: Lies on its side as it would rest on a bench: handle along Y, working end at +Y, lowest point on z = 0. Rotate to the hand for a held pose. The gooseneck lies flat with its claw pointing back toward the bar.
dimensions_note: Occupied extents of the voxel grid (X width, Y depth, Z height).
palette: Shared Claude palette v2 (tools/claude/voxkit.py); one material family per 8-swatch row in MagicaVoxel's palette grid.

grip.description: Main hand on the bar about a third of the way from the pry end.

collision_hint: Box matching dimensions_m, centred on the pivot.
story: A wrecking bar from a builder's van, used to pry open sheds, car boots and boarded doors. The dusty-red paint survives only along the middle of the bar; the hook and the pry end are rubbed back to dark steel.
notes: Hex-bar crowbar with a curved claw end and chipped dusty-red paint.
Height (Z) is the tool's real thickness lying on its side; the reference's larger Z is a coarse-cell minimum.

verification.magicavoxel_gui_open: unverified (MagicaVoxel not available in the build environment)
verification.godot_import: unverified (Godot not available in the build environment)
